_measured: 2026-09-19, cycle-12 W wiring commit — remeasured after the App.jsx lazy() conversion landed (eleven statically imported pages became their own chunks). Raw bytes from `bun run build` + `bun scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs` on the branch tree. entryChunkBytes 626643, entryChunkBrotliBytes 130294, firstPaintJsBytes 2306012 over 6 files, firstPaintCssBytes 1260054 over 2 render-blocking stylesheets, largestChunkBytes 4387670 (the vendor-logo chunk, loaded on demand), totalJsBytes 11470033, jsChunkCount 131. Before the conversion the same build measured entryChunkBytes 943354 / entryChunkBrotliBytes 186922 / firstPaintJsBytes 2622723 / jsChunkCount 105: the entry chunk lost 316711 raw bytes (56628 on the wire) and the count rose by 26, which is the trade the conversion is.
_policy: Budgets are the measurement plus 5%, rounded up. A build that exceeds one is not automatically wrong — but the raise belongs in the same commit as the weight, with the reason. The report also asks for a budget to be LOWERED once a measurement falls more than 20% under it.
_notJustJs: entryChunkBrotliBytes is what the visitor's connection actually carries, so weight that compresses well (locale tables, generated rows) cannot hide behind the raw-byte budgets. firstPaintCssBytes covers the two render-blocking stylesheets in <head>, which together are larger than the entry chunk they sit above — a .js-only budget could not see the biggest first-paint blocker double.
